_comment: MaterialBench SCENE DEFINITION — the MATERIAL DESIGNER (plan 92F0F90D S4): a node-graph editor over flicker-texture's v2 MaterialGraph. HEADER: the slot binding (the index dropdown) · the preset select (New, then every graph of the factory library, data/factory_materials.json, in file order) · Roll · Reseed · the designer ⇄ materials pages. LEFT the node list; CENTRE the graph canvas over the seven map views + the lit sample; RIGHT the selected node's parameters (one cell per node kind) over the output stage. FOOTER: bake rung · Commit · the status line. The `materialbench` behaviour plays it (flicker-materialbench); materialbench.lua derives the washes and the cell / page gates. Every control is a signal routed through the ONE dispatcher; nothing in Rust composes a control or injects a style.

params._comment_new_material: The NEW-material default — what the preset select's first entry (New) opens: one fBm noise driving the height, coloured through the neutral stone ramp. A v2 material graph document, authored as data; a malformed one is loud and New opens the factory library's first entry (data/factory_materials.json) instead — a blank graph when that library is empty too. Every number in it is Aaron's to tune.
params._comment_new_glow_strength: The strength a glow STARTS at when a glow colour is picked on a material that has none (the output stage's Glow select) — so the glow is visible the moment it exists. Aaron's to tune; a missing value is loud and falls back to the crate's own output-stage default.
params._comment_canvas_fit_floor: The graph canvas's READABLE zoom floor: a loaded graph (and Reset view) frames the whole graph only while that takes no smaller a zoom than this — below it the card titles and port labels are too small to read — and otherwise frames the selected node (or the Output card) at this zoom, the rest a pan away. Aaron's to tune; a missing value is loud and lets a fit zoom out to the canvas's own floor.

materialbench_lit._comment: The MaterialBench LIT PREVIEW — the material shown on a turning sample under a fixed light, which is the only way roughness/metalness/normal relief actually read. The `material` layer IS the sample body, drawn by the engine's material sample filler (flicker-materialview) in the seven preview maps the bench already holds (six bound — Height feeds no shading slot); the target clears TRANSPARENT so the node's panel supplies the backdrop, matching `portrait`.
materialbench_lit._emissive_gain: EMISSIVE GAIN — the draw-time multiplier on the material's Emit in this stage's HDR space (the bench hands it to the lit sample's maps). An 8-bit Emit texel caps at 1.0, so at 1.0 a glow never outshines the surface's own white and never crosses the bloom threshold; at 4.0 a full Emit texel burns at 4.0, past the threshold + knee below, so a glow reads as a glow — bloomed into a halo past the sample's edge — rather than as paint. The SAME 4.0 the Material Catalog's `mc_sample` authors, so a material glows alike in both (a gate holds the two equal). A finite number >= 0 (the stage compiler gates anything else). AARON'S TO TUNE in-window — a placeholder, never a Rust constant. The Emit COLOUR stays the material's own (the curated palette); this is only how bright it burns.
materialbench_lit._hdr: HDR: the `scene` pass (the lit material sample) renders into the LINEAR rgba16f `hdr` working attachment and `tonemap_grade` resolves it (ACES roll-off) into the sRGB `color` last, so specular highlights on metal/low-roughness roll off instead of clipping. grade_strength 0 = tonemap only, no invented tint — an art grade is Aaron's to author in-window. Alpha passes through, so the transparent clear the panel shows through survives.

passes._comment: BLOOM — what makes an EMISSIVE read as a glow: it reads the linear `hdr` the scene pass wrote, extracts everything above the threshold into a half-res buffer, blurs it, and ADDS the halo back into `hdr` — with the halo's coverage as alpha, so it shows past the body's edge over this TRANSPARENT clear. What crosses the threshold: a hot specular off low-roughness metal, and an Emit added over a lit surface at this stage's authored `emissive_gain` (4.0 above — a full Emit texel burns at 4.0, well past threshold + knee) — so it derives AFTER the scene pass (it reads `hdr`) and BEFORE `tonemap_grade` (which reads the bloomed `hdr` and rolls it off). No pass numbers anywhere — the reads/writes ARE the order. EVERY NUMBER BELOW IS AN ART PLACEHOLDER (pocclusters' values), tuned in-window, never in Rust: `threshold` ~1.0 is the brightness a pixel must exceed to bloom, so a lit matte surface (< 1.0) does not glow; `knee` is the soft shoulder below it so the glow fades in rather than popping on; `intensity` is how strongly the blurred glow is added back; `radius` scales the blur spread.

window._comment: This bench's root slab — scene-owned like populous's (a shared file would fork the look; duplication is the pattern). Only draw-read keys: no dead w/h.

select._comment: The header's dropdowns (the material binding, the preset) and the enum dials. `field` = the closed control; `menu` = the open popup rows. Data-driven options (the material names, the factory library's graph names from data/factory_materials.json, the glow palette) ride the Model through `label_bind`, never raw tree literals.

bar._comment: Header/footer band — a subtly raised slab so the top + bottom rows read as bars distinct from the body panels (UX pass may refine).

source_select._comment: The SOURCE selects — a port's input, an output port's driver. Tighter rows than the header's: a graph's field list can run long, and the menu opens downward from the field.

node_row._comment: A node-list row at rest (a `button` block — materialbench.lua washes the selected row with `node_row_sel`).
node_row.label: $ink

swatch._comment: A glow swatch's frame (the colour itself is the sprite inside); `swatch_sel` rings the one the glow wears.

canvas._comment: The graph canvas's colour slots (flicker_canvas::CanvasStyle). The filler owns no colour at all; every slot is a theme token here, resolved once when the bench enters.
canvas.label: $ink_bright

preview._comment: `tiles` = how many times the scene repeats the baked swatch per axis BEFORE uploading, so the seam shows in one sprite. Read by the Rust scene when it creates the preview textures.

nav_footer._comment: Bench nav rail band (like the Component Catalog's). `frame` = the node's own slab; `rule` (top hairline) + `label` (legend ink) + the `pad_glyphs` atlas resolve as the component's defaults.
nav_footer.label: $dim

children._comment: P5 informational tooltips (ruling 7AB130A7): a help strip for the designer's key ACTIONS. Informational name/meta only. Designer page only.

LEFT — the NODE LIST. A data-driven `list` over ONE button prototype (`rows_from: nodes`, CBF52F5C — the Component Catalog's breadcrumb recipe turned vertical): one row per node in the graph's node list, labelled `key · Kind` through `nl<i>_label`, picked by `nl_pick_<i>`, the selected row washed by materialbench.lua off `sel_node_index`. A bigger graph is more rows, never more tree. Insert opens the shared popup menu of node kinds; Delete takes the selected wire if one is picked on the canvas, else the selected node; Up / Down move it in the list (authoring order — the wires, not the list, decide evaluation).

CENTRE — the GRAPH CANVAS (flicker_canvas::GraphCanvas, seated in the `mtl_canvas` surface the walker reserves) above the seven-map swatch tabs and the lit sample. Cards are the nodes in evaluation order plus ONE output card (ports base · height · roughness · metalness · ao · glow colour · glow mask, down its right edge). Move drags cards (your arrangement, never the document); Link drags a card onto a port to wire it; a card pick selects its node, an edge pick selects that wire (Delete unwires it); the wheel zooms, a middle-drag pans.

The seven flat maps (each a `sprite` over its preview texture — `tex` 3..9, after the theme's own three in the HUD's table) and the LIT sample (the engine's material sample in the `mtl_lit` surface), exactly one shown at a time off `sel_map`. `size` is the well's height and the sprites' 300×300 is the swatch's drawn square — both Aaron's to tune.

The Lit view's ZOOM — how close the sample is drawn: the lit stage's camera distance divided by it (1 = the stage's own framing). The wheel over the sample moves the same number, one `step` per notch, inside this same range: the bench reads `min` / `max` / `step` from THIS node, the one source — no param repeats them. The zoom is the VIEW's: the body toggle and a material load keep it. AARON'S TO TUNE — placeholders: min 1.0, max 4.0, step 0.25. `min` must stay in (0, 1] and `max` at least 1 (the sample opens on the stage's framing) and `step` above 0; anything else switches the zoom off, loudly.
children.label: $mtl_lit_zoom

children._comment: RIGHT — the SELECTED NODE's parameters: one authored, `visible_bind`-gated cell PER NODE KIND (materialbench.lua shows exactly the one `sel_kind` names). Each lists only its kind's dials, bound `node_<param>` (sliders for numbers, selects for the enums, a toggle for invert), then one SOURCE select per input port bound `node_in<k>`: option 0 is none, then one option per row of `rows_from: in<k>` — only the nodes the graph would ACCEPT there (that port's kind of signal; never the node itself nor anything it feeds), so a pad can wire without the canvas and no option on offer is refused. Below them the OUTPUT STAGE (`rows_from: field` / `colour`). Every select repeats its LAST option (the prototype) after the ones authored ahead of it. Every slider range here is CONTENT — Aaron's to tune; the bench keeps the document valid (integers round, a non-finite value is refused) whatever a control writes.

The curated glow palette as SWATCHES — a data-driven `row` over ONE prototype (CBF52F5C): one cell per palette entry, each a `sprite` over the 1×1 texture the bench uploads for that colour (its texture slot rides the Model as `glow<i>_tex`). The swatch the glow wears is washed `materialbench.swatch_sel` by materialbench.lua. A legend, not a control: the glow colour is picked in the select above (one way to do it).
One row per DEFINED material (the index is data: a data-driven list over ONE button prototype, CBF52F5C). A row binds the graph to that slot (not an image edit).
What the status line's token is about — the node, port, parameter or loop a graph error names — as raw data beside the localized message.
